synopsis: A rainy night commute climbs out of the city, crosses a luminous spore layer and arrives on a bioluminescent moon under an enormous gas giant.

shots.prompt:
HOOK. Open already mid-motion on one ordinary object passing the glass at arm's length, so close and so fast it is only a streak. A dull, grey, utterly routine commute. At 1.5 seconds a two-note chime cuts in and a calm neutral announcer says the destination line. Nobody reacts and nothing changes. The train immediately accelerates hard. By 6 seconds ONE thing far ahead is unmistakably wrong, and it is already growing.

A rainy night commute through wet city outskirts. A petrol station forecourt slides past the glass close and fast, neon shop signs and bus shelters streaming backward, tower blocks stacked far behind, rain beading on the outside of the window. The announcer says exactly: "Next stop: Aloran." By 6 seconds the rain has stopped falling downward.

HARD BREACH. In the first half second something enormous slams past the glass at arm's length and blacks the frame out for an instant. Coming out of that darkness the ordinary world is already gone and the line has physically committed to the destination with no way back. The shot ends with the destination's first true landmark resolving far ahead.

A viaduct pier slams past the glass and blacks the frame. Out of it the rain is gone and individual luminous motes are drifting upward past the window instead. The last suburban lights shrink away below the track, the sky colour is wrong, and far ahead an unbroken blue-green glow already stands above the cloud line.

ARRIVAL EDGE. Open on a violent change of light in the first half second: the exposure blows out white or crushes to black and recovers. Then the first landmark grows continuously across the whole shot until it no longer fits inside the window. Show how far down or how far up the place goes. The scale must be frightening.

The train punches into a dense luminous spore layer and the exposure blows out blue-green. The carriage interior takes the colour. Then the layer thins and the window opens onto alien night under an enormous banded gas giant filling a third of the sky, a floating stone island trailing vines hanging far ahead above an unbroken cloud ocean, growing.

FLYTHROUGH. Open with that landmark's mass already passing the window at close range, filling the glass and strobing the interior. Maximum parallax: foreground elements cross the frame in a fraction of a second while the true size of the place is revealed by what lies beyond them. Something larger still is already visible ahead.

The floating island passes the window at close range, its vine curtains crossing the glass in a fraction of a second and its underside blotting out the gas giant. Waterfalls pour off the rock into cloud kilometres below. Beyond it a chain of far larger islands strung with bridges is already visible.

DEEPEST SCALE. Open with a hard impact against the glass in the first half second - heat, pressure, spray or a shockwave that jolts the camera and knocks the focus. Then the widest and deepest view of the destination so far, too large for the window to contain. The single most spectacular second of the episode belongs here.

Spray from a falling waterfall hits the glass, the camera jolts and the focus hunts. Then the widest view yet: island chains stacked into the distance above a luminous forest floor, and a colossal six-limbed animal gliding across the gas giant's pale bands, readable only by its scale against the islands.

HEART AND PAYOFF. Open with the train passing through or beneath something colossal. Travel alone carries it into the centre of the place. At about 8.5 seconds a calm ordinary commuter announcer quietly says the arrival line. Then the chime sounds again, the same voice begins only "Next stop-" and the shot ends mid-word while the train is still moving forward and something new is already growing ahead.

The train passes beneath a root arch so large its underside fills the entire window. Then the heart of the place: a single tree organism kilometres tall, bioluminescent settlements and suspended platforms glowing among its branches, tiny figures moving on high spans, deeper canopy lights beyond. The announcer says exactly: "Welcome to Aloran."
